text:
Lena O: Idea: plant-tag thank-you drop next Thursday. small paper tags tied to office plants with a 1-line note to a teammate. low-cost, tactile, and spreads around the office.
Ava (People Ops): Interesting! very on-brand. What supplies and timing?
Lena O: Tags (pre-printed prompt), baker's twine, clothespins, and a tray to stage them. Aim for lunchtime 12:00-1:00 for max passersby.
Marco H: Facilities can help hang tags on common-area plants. We can do 8 large plants across floors. Need lead time to borrow a small ladder.
Zoe K: I'll design the back prompt: "To:\nFrom:\nWhy I appreciate you: (one line)" Keep it small so people write quickly.
Lena O: Budget ask: ~$60 for cardstock + twine + pens. Ava, ok to charge to events code?
Ava (People Ops): Sounds fine. Submit PO and I'll route to finance. Try to keep it internal print to save time.
FacilitiesBot: Ladder/step stool reserve requested: ticket #6677. ETA approval 1 business day.
KudosBot: Suggestion: add a tiny sticker for each tag so recipients know it's official. I can provide 150 stickers.
Marco H: Good call. Also suggest a small note for managers asking them to encourage teams to participate during lunch.
Zoe K: I'll make the tag art and a 1-line poster for the plant table that says: "Leave a one-line thank-you on a tag. We'll attach it to a plant and route it later."
Ava (People Ops): Runbook please: pickup location, setup time (11:30), volunteers (2), collection plan (drop at Mailroom by 3pm). Lena, can you own volunteers?
Lena O: Yes. Volunteers: me (11:30-12:30) and Marco (12:00-1:00). Need one more for 12:30-1:00.
Ava (People Ops): I'll post volunteer ask in #general. Also will queue manager nudge with sample line. PO approved pending receipt. Finance typically clears within a business day.
Lena O: Cool. I'll upload tag PDF and runbook here tonight. Also planning a short feedback poll after to see if people liked physical tags vs digital notes.
KudosBot: Reminder set: collect stickers and extras at 1:05pm and drop to Mailroom by 2:30pm.
Ava (People Ops): Love this low-lift experiment. If all goes well, we can expand plant coverage or try seasonal variants. :seedling:
